meta.title: VAT / GST on prescription veterinary medicines sold at retail
meta.why: Shelf prices in Europe, the UK, Türkiye and Australia are quoted tax-inclusive; US shelf prices are quoted ex-tax. Comparing them raw flatters the US. Dividing each tax-inclusive price by (1 + rate) puts every market on an ex-tax basis.
meta.trap: Many countries give HUMAN medicines a reduced rate and leave VETERINARY medicines at the standard rate - and several do the opposite. The rate that matters here is the veterinary one, which is why every row below is sourced on veterinary-specific wording wherever such wording exists.
meta.scope: Retail sale of the medicine AS GOODS (online or bricks-and-mortar pharmacy). Where a vet dispenses from the practice dispensary as part of a clinical act, several countries (ES, NL, PT) tax the whole invoice at the standard rate as an ancillary supply. Clinic-administered rows are excluded from the comparison for that reason, among others.
meta.method: Every tax-authority domain tried was blocked by this environment's egress proxy (gov.uk, bofip.impots.gouv.fr, belastingdienst.nl, agenciatributaria.gob.es, financnasprava.sk, nrsr.sk). Rates therefore rest on search-engine extraction of those pages plus corroborating professional sources, cross-checked between two independent research passes that agreed on every row. They are not a reading of the statutes from an unrestricted connection.

confidence.HIGH: veterinary-specific wording found in, or quoted from, the statute or the tax authority's own guidance
confidence.MEDIUM: no veterinary-specific wording found; rate follows by elimination or from a tariff-code reference

GB.law: VATA 1994 Sch 8 Grp 12 - the zero rate for dispensed drugs is confined to goods dispensed to an individual for that individual's personal use, so animal prescriptions never qualify

DE.law: UStG Anlage 2 contains no medicines entry at all; human and veterinary medicines alike fall to the §12(1) standard rate

NL.law: Belastingdienst publishes a dedicated ruling page 'Btw-tarief diergeneesmiddelen' placing veterinary medicines sold as goods in the 9% bracket; 21% applies only when a vet administers the medicine as part of treatment

FR.law: Art. 278 quater CGI limits the 10% rate to products for human medicine; France has not taken up the EU option to extend it to veterinary medicines

IT.law: Tabella A parte III n. 114, DPR 633/1972: 'medicinali pronti per l'uso umano o veterinario' - veterinary use named in the statute itself

ES.law: Art. 91.Uno.1.5 LIVA (Ley 37/1992) - medicamentos de uso animal at 10%. DGT binding ruling V0967-24 (6 May 2024) puts the whole invoice at 21% only when a vet hands the medicine over as part of a clinical act; an online pharmacy selling goods stays at 10%

PT.law: Verba 2.5 a) da Lista I anexa ao CIVA; AT binding information confirms the transmission of veterinary medicines takes the reduced rate (23% if the invoice does not separate medicine from consultation)
PT.unused: no Portuguese venue currently in the panel

CZ.law: Priloha c. 3 zakona c. 235/2004 Sb. (from 1 Jan 2024) covers medicines 'pro humanni a veterinarni lekarske ucely' - veterinary use named explicitly

SK.law: Priloha c. 7 bod 3 zak. 222/2004: 'lieky a farmaceuticke vyrobky - cela kapitola 30 colneho sadzobnika'. Customs chapter 30 covers medicaments for therapeutic or prophylactic use without a human/veterinary distinction, so veterinary medicines follow at 5%
SK.flag: inferred from a tariff-code reference, not from veterinary-specific wording. The standard rate is 23%, so if the inference is wrong Slovakia is understated here by 17 points - the widest unresolved uncertainty in this table

HU.law: The 5% list in 3. mellek let of the Afa tv. is restricted to medicines 'emberi alkalmazasra kerulo' (for human use); veterinary preparations stay at the 27% standard rate. Hungary moves prescription HUMAN medicines to 0% from 1 Sep 2026 - veterinary is explicitly excluded from that too

RO.law: Law 141/2025, in force 1 Aug 2025, DELETED veterinary medicines from art. 291(2)(c) Cod fiscal. Human medicines went 9% to 11%; veterinary medicines went 9% to the full 21% standard rate

BG.law: The 9% reduced list contains no medicines category at all (accommodation, books, baby food and nappies only), so medicines follow the 20% standard rate by elimination

TR.law: Decree 2007/13033 List (II) section B item 20: veterinary pharmaceutical and medicinal preparations licensed by the Ministry of Agriculture, veterinary cosmetics excluded. Raised 8% to 10% by Presidential Decree 7346 from 10 Jul 2023; standard rate is 20%

AU.law: The GST-free drug provisions (GST Act 1999 s.38-50, Subdiv 38-B Health) require supply to an individual for private or domestic use under human-medicines law; APVMA-regulated veterinary products are taxable. Australian consumer prices must by law be displayed GST-inclusive

US.law: US retail prices are quoted before sales tax by universal convention, so the listed price is already the ex-tax price. Whether a state then taxes the sale varies - most states extend their prescription-drug exemption to animal prescriptions, New Jersey taxes pet prescriptions, New York depends on whether the seller is a vet or a pharmacy - but none of that is inside the number a US site displays
